themes.name: AI compute: NVIDIA's supply chain
themes.what: Amazon kept its $220 billion 2026 capex plan, spent $77.3 billion in Q3 against $58.7 billion expected, and said it will spend 'meaningfully more' in 2027; AWS grew 39% but trailing free cash flow was negative $42.4 billion, and the stock was down 6% to 7% premarket (CNBC). Intel guided Q4 revenue to $15 billion to $16 billion against $17.1 billion expected and was down about 24% premarket. Marvell closed down 13.24% at 218.34 on reports of an all stock Lumentum deal (Massive, Motley Fool).
themes.for_you: The spending keeps rising, which supports chip and memory suppliers, but buyers punish spenders that burn cash. No new AI buys into a 2% Nasdaq gap down; MRVL sits at the bottom of its 218.02 to 251.36 zone, but wait for deal terms.

themes.name: AI power and the grid
themes.what: Correction: Microsoft cut its capex forecast for the year to $170 billion from $175 billion, and both Microsoft and Alphabet capex fell short of estimates (CNBC, Oct 29); an earlier entry read the $170 billion as a 2027 increase. Amazon said it will spend 'meaningfully more' in 2027 (CNBC). The ECB's Lagarde said hyperscaler bond issuance is helping push long term borrowing costs up worldwide (CNBC).
themes.for_you: Power demand still grows, but slower than the bulls assumed for Microsoft. Left out of both lists: one spender trimmed, another raised. No new power buys into the Nov 3 vote.

themes.name: Critical materials and geopolitics
themes.what: Rio Tinto said it has begun restarting underground operations at its Oyu Tolgoi copper mine in Mongolia after a seismic event halted mining (Reuters, Oct 30).
themes.for_you: No action. A restart adds copper supply back; RIO and FCX are not setups.

themes.name: Defense, drones and reshoring
themes.what: Boeing bounced 3.30% to 172.65 on Oct 29 on 16.76 million shares, about twice its normal volume (Massive), as dip buyers stepped in after two heavy selling days (TradingKey). Defense primes rose the same day: GD 4.65% to 370.82, LMT 2.20% and NOC 1.73% (Massive).
themes.for_you: No action on BA: it is 'Avoid' and one bounce does not reverse two heavy down days. LMT showed on the MT Breakout Trigger scan Oct 29, but defense primes have no swing setup on the dashboard.

themes.name: Fintech and Crypto Rails: Stablecoins, Tokenization, Exchanges
themes.what: Binance said a security breach had an estimated $6.3 billion impact, with about $3 billion frozen, and pledged to cover losses; Circle and Tether froze a combined $2.54 billion, and bitcoin fell below $78,000 (CNBC, Oct 30). Mastercard rose 4.16% to 635.70 and Visa 2.48% to 410.54 on Oct 29 after Mastercard's Q3 beat (Massive, briefs.co).
themes.for_you: MA closed 5.8% above its 517.30 to 601.09 zone: no buy at this price. Crypto names are a pass while hack fallout settles. CRCL is left out of both lists: freezing stolen funds shows control, but crypto volumes may fall.

themes.name: GLP-1 and obesity
themes.what: WST confirmed its swing breakout on Oct 29: it closed at 416.67, above the 398.67 pivot, on 1,873,146 shares, 3.35 times its 50 day average, the day after its beat and raise (Massive). It traded as high as 438.27 before fading under its 420.69 open.
themes.for_you: Swing: WST passed her volume rule. Buy only near the pivot, not after a run; it closed 4.5% above 398.67. Long term it stays Wait, far above its 210.80 to 285.20 zone.

themes.name: Healthcare and Medtech: Aging, Heart, Sugar, Hearing, Sight
themes.what: Dexcom's Q3 revenue rose 11% to $1.3445 billion and it raised its 2026 revenue guide to $5.20 billion to $5.25 billion, with higher margin guidance (company release, Oct 29). AstraZeneca beat with $16.2 billion of Q3 revenue and core EPS of $2.79 against $2.59 expected (CNBC, Oct 30). The FDA panel on Sydnexis's SYD-101 child myopia drop meets Oct 30.
themes.for_you: DXCM closed at 79.93 on Oct 29, inside its 72.22 to 84.70 zone, but the verdict is 'Buy zone, wait for the chart'; let the post report reaction settle. No put until the chart check passes.

themes.name: Robotics, Automation and Physical AI
themes.what: North American robot orders rose 25% in Q3 2026, and collaborative robots reached 1,831 units worth $63.8 million, up about 56% in units from a year earlier (Metrology News, Oct 30).
themes.for_you: No action. ZBRA is on the MT Swing Setup list and closed at 377.38 on Oct 29, just under its 378.08 zone top on Oct 28 data (Massive).

innovations.name: Consumer
innovations.what: Rotation recheck. EssilorLuxottica's Q3 wearables revenue was 486 million euros, up 20% but a sharp slowdown in smart glasses growth (Reuters, Oct 20). Dexcom's Q3 revenue rose 11% to $1.3445 billion and it raised its 2026 guide to $5.20 billion to $5.25 billion (Oct 29). The FDA panel on SYD-101 meets Oct 30 with FDA doubts on the data (Pink Sheet). Oura still has no IPO date. No stage moves.
innovations.for_you: DXCM closed at 79.93 on Oct 29, inside its 72.22 to 84.70 zone, but the verdict is 'Buy zone, wait for the chart'. META and ESLOY are left out of both lists: glasses still grow, just slower. No action.

countries.name: Argentina
countries.what: The Merval fell 1% to 94,530 on Oct 29, a fourth straight loss, while dollar bonds rebounded and country risk eased under 750 points (Ambito). In New York YPF fell 3.10% to 47.81 and ARGT 1.03% to 81.48 (Massive).
countries.for_you: No action. No Argentine stock is on the buy zone list; YPF tracks oil more than Buenos Aires.

countries.name: Brazil
countries.what: Day four of the post election slide: the Ibovespa fell 1.06% to 169,186 on Oct 29 and the dollar rose 0.76% to R$5.39 (Agencia Brasil). Correction to earlier entries: the pre election Focus survey expected a Selic cut in November, and after the vote analysts debate a pause; a hike is one view, not the consensus (Folha, Estadao). US closes Oct 29: EWZ 33.14, NU 12.05, ITUB 7.37, BBD 2.63, PBR 21.90 (Massive).
countries.for_you: No action. NU is 8.0% under its 13.10 line. The real weakening again is the warning sign; wait for Nov 4.

countries.name: China
countries.what: The CSI 300 fell 1.39% to 3,985.50 on Oct 30 as global tech sold off, while the Hang Seng rose about 1.5% late in the session (CNBC). The yuan midpoint was set at 6.7138 (TMGM).
countries.for_you: No action. FXI closed at 32.69 on Oct 29 (Massive). Left out of both lists: Hong Kong rose while the mainland fell.

countries.name: European Union
countries.what: The ECB held at 2.5% on Oct 29 and said a hike was debated; markets price about a 67% chance of a December hike. Lagarde will step down Feb 7, 2027. France's Q3 GDP fell 0.1%, and December Dutch gas rose to 101.63 euros on Oct 30, the highest since late 2022 (CNBC).
countries.for_you: No action. Expensive gas into winter is a headwind for European stocks (EZU 66.23 on Oct 29, Massive). Energy producers gain.

countries.name: Gulf (Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar, Iran risk)
countries.what: A tanker in the Strait of Hormuz was hit by explosive devices on Oct 30, Houthi rebels claimed strikes on Saudi refineries at Ras Tanura and Rabigh and a site at Abqaiq, and Brent rose 2.4% to $117.62 (Reuters). Gulf exports are above pre war levels (Kpler via Al Jazeera). Exxon and Chevron cancelled executive trips to next week's ADIPEC show in Abu Dhabi (Reuters).
countries.for_you: XOM and CVX are at or near their 2R targets; take the plan. Airlines (DAL, UAL) pay for higher jet fuel.

countries.name: India
countries.what: The Nifty rose 0.51% to 23,053.10 and the Sensex 0.42% to 74,459.53 on Oct 30, led by IT and pharma, while other Asian markets fell; Infosys rose 2.70% (Business Line, ET Now). Reserves fell a seventh straight week (Reuters).
countries.for_you: No action. Rising oil is the risk to watch for INDA; IT exporters gain from a weak rupee.

countries.name: Japan
countries.what: The BOJ held at 1.25% on Oct 30 with one dissent for a hike and said inflation is now 'generally consistent' with 2%, its first such call since 2013. The Nikkei fell 2.12% to 63,290.11 as chip equipment names sold off after Amazon and Intel (CNBC).
countries.for_you: No action. A December hike is now likely; that firms the yen and helps the banks.

countries.name: Mexico
countries.what: The peso fell 1.2% to about 18.86 per dollar on Oct 29 after strong US growth and inflation data, and Banxico's Borja defended the 6.50% rate (TMGM). Q3 GDP is due Oct 30.
countries.for_you: No action. EWW closed at 74.47 on Oct 29 (Massive); none of these names is a setup.

countries.name: South Korea
countries.what: The KOSPI fell 3.48% to 5,730.74 on Oct 30 after Amazon and Intel results, with SK hynix down about 6.4% and Samsung about 3.5% during the session (CNBC). The Roundhill Memory ETF is down 14% in October (CNBC).
countries.for_you: No action. Memory is falling on AI spending fears, not on weaker demand; wait for the selling to stop before any memory trade.

countries.name: Taiwan
countries.what: The Taiex fell 2.49% to 45,211.83 on Oct 30 after Amazon and Intel results, with a net NT$112.47 billion of foreign selling; TSMC fell 1.86% to NT$2,370 (Focus Taiwan). Trading Economics showed an intraday low near 44,922; the close from Focus Taiwan is used.
countries.for_you: No action. EWT closed at 105.99 on Oct 29 (Massive). Wait for foreign selling to ease.
